diagnostic_evidence.quote: each particle is effectively discretized with a sufficiently high number of pixels $\bm{y}_j$ with volume $1/M$.
A drawback of our discretization procedure is that there is generally no Monge map between two discrete measures.

issues.failure_explanation: The hard map assigns each pixel wholly to one cell, so every resulting cell volume is an integer multiple of 1/M. For general input volumes v_i, including any v_i not of that form, no such map can satisfy the prescribed marginals. Entropic transport potentials and pointwise argmin assignment do not remove this integrality obstruction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either retain a mass-splitting transport plan or add an allocation/rounding procedure with a proved error bound, and weaken the strict-volume guarantee to the resulting discretization accuracy when exact masses are impossible.
issues.overall_effect: The implemented discrete shapes do not in general satisfy the paper's advertised strict individual volume constraints; they only approximate them at pixel resolution and may also be affected by ties.
issues.title: The hard pixel allocation cannot enforce arbitrary prescribed volumes
issues.why_classification: Every available repair either changes the hard shape representation or withdraws the central strict-volume guarantee for the actual numerical method.

With f=-delta_+, the cost is therefore increased in directions of positive chemo-attractant gradient, so fixed-cost sublevel shapes contract rather than protrude there and their barycenter is biased oppositely. The same sign error makes the negative Gaussian perturbations produce indentations rather than the claimed random protrusions.
